movies.title: Le Manoir du Diable (1896) by Georges Méliès
movies.description: Georges Méliès' 1896 silent film "The House of the Devil" is the first horror film in existence. Like most of his work during this period, Méliès milked the horror premise for comedy and spectacle, experimenting with trick photography and visual illusions. Even back then, "The House of the Devil" had all the horror movie clichés before they were clichés: demons, skeletons, ghosts, witchcraft, sorcery, and a spooky gothic castle. All in just 3 minutes! The film's original French title is "Le Manoir du diable." The film is sometimes confused with its remake "The Haunted Castle" (1897) (French: "Le Château hanté").
movies.creator: Georges Méliès

movies.title: Le Voyage Dans La Lune
movies.description: Le Voyage Dans La Lune is a 1902 French science fiction black and white film. It is loosely based on two popular novels of the time: From the Earth to the Moon by Jules Verne and The First Men in the Moon by H. G. Wells. It was written and directed by Georges Méliès, with help from his brother Gaston. It is recognized as one of the first films of the science fiction genre, and for its innovative animation. This version is narrated in French and the end has been edited/cut until the beginning of the celebratory scene.
movies.creator: Georges Méliès (December 8, 1861 – January 21, 1938) and Gaston Méliès (1845 - April 1915)

movies.title: A Fool and His Money (1912)
movies.description: A Fool and His Money is a ten-minute black-and-white silent narrative that is the first American film to have an entire cast of Black actors. Not only that, it was produced and directed by Alice Guy-Blaché, the first female filmmaker in the history of cinema. It's also considered one of the earliest race films–a genre produced in the United States between 1912 and the 1950s, aimed at primarily Black audiences.

shows.description: NASA Explorers: science, engineering and space exploration from NASA’s own video library. Browse the available episodes by season or year.

episodes.title: NASA Explorers S4 E1: Orbiting Laboratory
episodes.description: jsc2019m001193 - Things behave a bit differently aboard the International Space Station, thanks to microgravity. Sure, floating looks like fun, but it could also unlock new scientific discoveries. Microgravity makes the station the perfect place to perform research that is changing the lives of people on Earth, and preparing us to go deeper into space. This season on #NASAExplorers, we are following science into low-Earth orbit and seeing what it takes to do research aboard the space station. See more NASA Explorers season 4 bonus content here: https://go.nasa.gov/2FKavmn #S4E1
episodes.creator: NASA / JSC

episodes.title: NASA Explorers S4 E2: The Scientists
episodes.description: jsc2019m001195 - Putting your life’s work on top of a rocket may seem like a daunting task, but that’s exactly what scientists have been doing for decades as they launch their research to the International Space Station. This season on #NASAExplorers, we’re exploring why we send science to space, and what it takes to get it there. Spoiler alert: you don’t have to be a rocket scientist to conduct research in microgravity. This week, meet a team of researchers who are launching an experiment to space for the first time. See more NASA Explorers season 4 bonus content here: https://go.nasa.gov/2FKavmn Stay up to date with ISS Research on Twitter: https://twitter.com/ISS_Research #S4E2
episodes.creator: NASA / JSC

episodes.title: NASA Explorers S4 E3: Training the Astronauts
episodes.description: jsc2019m001196 - Astronauts train all over the world, including at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston, Texas. Here, they learn not just how to live in space, but also how to conduct science in microgravity. Astronauts serve as the eyes and hands of researchers while their experiments are aboard the space station, so they must be trained in everything from using a microscope, to maintaining the equipment for combustion experiments. Follow along with #NASAExplorers as we go to class with NASA astronaut Mike Fincke. See more NASA Explorers season 4 bonus content here: https://go.nasa.gov/2FKavmn Stay up to date with ISS Research on Twitter: https://twitter.com/ISS_Research #S4E3
episodes.creator: NASA / JSC

episodes.title: NASA Explorers S4 E4: Before the Rocket
episodes.description: jsc2019m001197 - Our team of scientists is just days away from their research being loaded onto a SpaceX rocket that will carry their experiment to the International Space Station. This week on #NASAExplorers, we are following along with them in the busy days leading up to launch at Kennedy Space Center, as they do all of the last-minute preparations to get their experiment ready for microgravity. See more NASA Explorers season 4 bonus content: https://go.nasa.gov/2FKavmn Stay up to date with ISS Research on Twitter: https://twitter.com/ISS_Research Watch all NASA Explorers season 4 episodes: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL2aBZuCeDwlQDM6x6FpHE_X0iL7hvoRpR
episodes.creator: NASA / JSC

episodes.title: NASA Explorers S4 E5: Journey to Space
episodes.description: jsc2019m001198 - The day has finally arrived. After years of work, our team of scientists is at the Kennedy Space Center in the hopes of seeing their research liftoff to the International Space Station. Join us this week on NASA Explorers for the countdown, the emotion and, hopefully, the launch. See more NASA Explorers season 4 bonus content: https://go.nasa.gov/2FKavmn Stay up to date with ISS Research on Twitter: https://twitter.com/ISS_Research Watch all NASA Explorers season 4 episodes: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL2aBZuCeDwlQDM6x6FpHE_X0iL7hvoRpR
episodes.creator: NASA / JSC

episodes.title: NASA Explorers S4 E6: On Station
episodes.description: jsc2019m001199 - Now that our researchers’ experiment is on the International Space Station, it’s time to test how their samples behave in microgravity. This week on NASA Explorers, the astronauts conduct science in space, while a team back here on Earth runs their own piece of the project. See more NASA Explorers season 4 bonus content: https://go.nasa.gov/2FKavmn Stay up to date with ISS Research on Twitter: https://twitter.com/ISS_Research Watch all NASA Explorers season 4 episodes: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL2aBZuCeDwlQDM6x6FpHE_X0iL7hvoRpR
episodes.creator: NASA / JSC

episodes.title: NASA Explorers S4 E7: On Station
episodes.description: jsc2019m001200 - With the experiment’s journey complete, Elaine Horn-Ranney Ph.D. and Parastoo Khoshaklagh Ph.D. now join the thousands of scientists who’ve performed research aboard the International Space Station, making the most of what microgravity has to teach us. Although the thrill of the rocket launch may be over, our scientists still have one of the most exciting parts of their journey ahead: sharing their results with the world. See more NASA Explorers season 4 bonus content: https://go.nasa.gov/2FKavmn Stay up to date with ISS Research on Twitter: https://twitter.com/ISS_Research Watch all NASA Explorers season 4 episodes: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL2aBZuCeDwlQDM6x6Fp
episodes.creator: NASA / JSC

episodes.title: NASA Explorers S4 E8: 20 Years of Science
episodes.description: This season on NASA Explorers, you’ve seen what it takes to send science to the International Space Station through the eyes of one team of researchers. They are just two of thousands more scientists who have sent experiments to the orbiting laboratory over the past two decades. Take a look back at those 20 years of microgravity science along with the researchers who helped make it happen. Hear more from the researchers featured in this episode: https://go.nasa.gov/327KMjI
episodes.creator: NASA / JSC

shows.title: NASA ScienceCasts
shows.description: NASA ScienceCasts: science, engineering and space exploration from NASA’s own video library. Browse the available episodes by season or year.

episodes.title: ScienceCasts: Space Gardening
episodes.description: Scientists have been studying plant growth on the International Space Station. The results could help boost the productivity of both extraterrestrial and earthly gardens.
episodes.creator: NASA / HQ

episodes.title: ScienceCasts: The Mystery of High-Energy Cosmic Rays
episodes.description: The cosmic ray detector known as CREAM is headed for the International Space Station, with a goal of measuring the highest energy possible for direct measurement of high-energy cosmic rays.
episodes.creator: NASA / HQ

episodes.title: NASA ScienceCasts: Thinking Inside the Box
episodes.description: Gloveboxes on the ISS allow for experiments on materials that you wouldn't want escaping into the station's enclosed space.
episodes.creator: NASA / HQ

episodes.title: NASA ScienceCasts: A Super Start to 2019
episodes.description: 2019 is an excellent year to look to the sky and enjoy the spectacular view of Earth’s nearest neighbor, the Moon.
episodes.creator: NASA / HQ

episodes.title: NASA ScienceCasts: The Space We Travel Through
episodes.description: As NASA prepares to send astronauts and spacecraft long distances through space, scientists are keeping an eye on the weather. Space weather.
episodes.creator: NASA / HQ

episodes.title: NASA ScienceCasts: A Successful Mission Starts With Nutrition
episodes.description: The relationship between a successful exploration mission and balanced nutrition is vital in the extreme vastness of outer space.
episodes.creator: NASA / HQ

episodes.title: NASA ScienceCasts: On the Cusp of Understanding
episodes.description: NASA is using sounding rockets to study the cusp, a point where the magnetic bubble that surrounds our planet dips inward and touches down to Earth.
episodes.creator: NASA / HQ

episodes.title: NASA ScienceCasts: A Chip off the Old Block
episodes.description: Living 3D versions of human organs called Tissue Chips are being sent to the International Space Station to be studied in microgravity.
episodes.creator: NASA / HQ

episodes.title: NASA ScienceCasts: Shining Laser Light on Earth’s Forests
episodes.description: The Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation (GEDI) on the space station beams laser light down to Earth to reveal the height and density of trees and vegetation.
episodes.creator: NASA / HQ

episodes.title: NASA ScienceCasts: Cementing Our Place in Space
episodes.description: Experiments have taken place aboard the International Space Station to study cement based concrete in microgravity.
episodes.creator: NASA / HQ

episodes.title: NASA ScienceCasts: Watch the History of our Solar System Fly By with MU69
episodes.description: Scientists are unlocking clues about the earliest formation of our solar system from a Kuiper Belt Object known as 2014 MU69.
episodes.creator: NASA / HQ

episodes.title: NASA ScienceCasts: The Lasting Impacts of Comet Shoemaker-Levy 9
episodes.description: In July 1994, astronomers around the world watched as the fragments of comet Shoemaker-Levy 9 slammed into the planet Jupiter.
episodes.creator: NASA / HQ

episodes.title: NASA ScienceCasts: Cutting-edge Biomanufacturing Aboard the International Space Station
episodes.description: Welcome to the world of 3D biomanufacturing, a cutting-edge practice on Earth that is being tested aboard the International Space Station.
episodes.creator: NASA / HQ

episodes.title: NASA ScienceCasts: Shedding Light on Black Holes
episodes.description: "Black Holes" is one of the most highly searched terms about our universe. How much of what we think we know about black holes is actually true?
episodes.creator: NASA / HQ

episodes.title: NASA ScienceCasts: Eye on Neptune
episodes.description: Neptune will be at opposition in September, providing sky watchers and astronomers the opportunity to observe this planet that is invisible to the naked eye, but that scientists would love to see more clearly.
episodes.creator: NASA / HQ

episodes.title: NASA ScienceCasts: Unlocking the Origins of the Universe
episodes.description: AMS-02 is helping scientists investigate many fundamental physics questions from its place on the space station. Astronauts are conducting a series of spacewalks to perform repairs and extend the life of the observatory.
episodes.creator: NASA / HQ

episodes.title: NASA ScienceCasts: Effects of the Solar Wind
episodes.description: The continuously expanding solar wind begins in our Sun and doesn’t stop until after it reaches the edge of the heliosphere.
episodes.creator: NASA / HQ

episodes.title: NASA ScienceCasts: Making Space for Technology Development
episodes.description: The International Space Station provides the only microgravity environment in which we can test technologies critical to our deep-space exploration in the near and far-term future.
episodes.creator: NASA / HQ

episodes.title: NASA ScienceCasts: Finding the Invisible
episodes.description: Scientists are using AMS-02 on the Space Station to study fundamental particles originating from sources up to billions of light years away. These particles may hold the key to understanding both the composition and history of our universe.
episodes.creator: NASA / HQ

episodes.title: NASA ScienceCasts: Keeping an Eye on Earth
episodes.description: Earth observing instruments on the space station along with photography from crew members serve to keep a multifunctional eye on our home planet.
episodes.creator: NASA / HQ

episodes.title: NASA ScienceCasts: A Growing Market at Gravity’s Edge
episodes.description: The commercialization of low-Earth orbit is enabling a new market in space, while aiding NASA in its mission of exploration and discovery.
episodes.creator: NASA / HQ

episodes.title: NASA ScienceCasts: The Small Satellite That’s Paying Big Dividends
episodes.description: NASA ScienceCasts: The Small Satellite That’s Paying Big Dividends
episodes.creator: NASA / HQ

episodes.title: NASA ScienceCasts: Observing Lightning from the International Space Station
episodes.description: Colorful bursts of energy above thunderstorms called transient luminous events can be observed from the International Space Station. Instruments on the station are helping scientists study these particle outbursts, which may prove useful to better understand our climate, weather, and the behaviors of storms.
episodes.creator: NASA / HQ

episodes.title: NASA ScienceCasts: Doing Business in Space
episodes.description: The International Space Station is a one-of-a-kind laboratory, allowing for experiments in microgravity conditions that couldn’t be duplicated on Earth. It has also proven to have the capacity to serve as an incubator for new business, accelerating the development of a new space economy in low-Earth orbit.
episodes.creator: NASA / HQ

episodes.title: NASA ScienceCasts: The Power of the Station's New Solar Arrays
episodes.description: The new ISS Roll Out Solar Arrays (iROSA) being installed on the space station are providing power to the station with improved efficiency. ROSA technology will also help power the Gateway lunar outpost, and the DART mission as it makes its way to the Didymos asteroid system.
episodes.creator: NASA / HQ

episodes.title: NASA ScienceCasts: Teeming Life on the ISS
episodes.description: A cornucopia of species bring the interior of the International Space Station to life, and also bring a plethora of scientific knowledge contributing to humans thriving both on Earth and beyond the edge of our planet.
episodes.creator: NASA / HQ

episodes.title: NASA ScienceCasts: T2AR on the ISS
episodes.description: T2 is one of the station’s treadmill. AR is augmented reality. And NASA is using its treadmill to test how crew members can use AR to make repairs in space.
episodes.creator: NASA / HQ

episodes.title: NASA ScienceCasts: Observing Change Over Time
episodes.description: To date, over 4 million photos taken by humans from space have been collected. These photographs are taken for many purposes, from artistic to the scientific, and have proven to have a wide range of uses.
episodes.creator: NASA / HQ

episodes.title: NASA ScienceCasts: Vision Changes in Space
episodes.description: Scientists are working hard to better understand why vision changes occur for some astronauts in microgravity, while continuously developing strategies to counter those changes.
episodes.creator: NASA / HQ

episodes.title: NASA ScienceCasts: Water Recovery on the Space Station
episodes.description: NASA now has the ability to recycle 98% of the water collected from the US segment on the space station – meeting the threshold necessary for water recovery on long-duration space exploration missions.
episodes.creator: NASA / JSC

episodes.title: NASA ScienceCasts: The CIPHER Project
episodes.description: NASA’s new Human Research Program project, CIPHER, integrates 14 multi-disciplinary investigations and examines multiple astronauts across different mission durations over the course of many years. CIPHER: www.nasa.gov/CHIPER
episodes.creator: NASA / HQ

episodes.title: NASA ScienceCasts: ECLSS on Station
episodes.description: The International Space Station’s Environmental Control and Life Support System, known as ECLSS, provides clean air and water to the crew -- making life aboard the Space Station possible.
episodes.creator: NASA / HQ

episodes.title: NASA ScienceCasts: Station Science 101 - Advancing Plant Science with Space Gardens
episodes.description: Gardens growing on the International Space Station are leading to groundbreaking research and offering astronauts a taste of home. Station Science 101: Plant Growth - Feature http://go.nasa.gov/4e57lJ2
episodes.creator: NASA / HQ

episodes.title: NASA ScienceCasts: Station Science 101 - Earth Observation from the Space Station
episodes.description: Stunning images of Earth captured by crew members on the International Space Station are actively supporting life on our planet, helping monitor climate change, and advancing our understanding of Earth’s changing landscapes.
episodes.creator: NASA / HQ

episodes.title: NASA ScienceCasts: Station Science 101 - Growing Space Crystals to Improve Medicine
episodes.description: The International Space Station could help develop new and better drugs for people on Earth, thanks to protein crystal growth, or PCG, on board.
episodes.creator: NASA / HQ

episodes.title: NASA ScienceCasts: Station Science 101 - Monitoring Microbes for Astronaut Health
episodes.description: Protecting astronauts on the International Space Station from harmful pathogens is leading to groundbreaking advancements in microbiology. Feature: https://www.nasa.gov/missions/station/microbiology-101-where-people-go-microbes-follow/
episodes.creator: NASA / JSC
